messages:
incident-bot: PAGED maria-oncall due to SLO breach: eu-west2 p99 generation latency > 3s for 6m. automated alert: route-telemetry indicates 12% of traffic hitting routers with >200ms queueing. paging policy: severity=page

maria-oncall: on it. joining bridge. any customer-facing impact yet?

ops-alerts: trend snapshot:
- p95 jumped from 220ms -> 760ms
- p99 jumped from 430ms -> 3.4s
- streaming stalls: ~0.8% of active streams reported >10s token stalls
- source: ingress -> router pool euw2-a -> 2 of 8 routers with sustained qdepth >80

maria-oncall: alex-runtime can you confirm router-side queueing? is this LB or router?

alex-runtime: seeing a routing weight drift in the config service. recent rollout id=cfg-2026-03-14-evict-affinity pushed an ingress affinity tweak. many clients are being funneled to a small subset of sharded routers (hot shards). logs: 
```
2026-03-15T09:12:03Z WARN router[euw2-a-03]: queue_depth=92 applied_weight=0.12 expected=0.02
2026-03-15T09:12:11Z WARN lb[euw2]: reject_backpressure=0.01 forwarded_to=euw2-a-03
```

dan-sre: looks like rollout changed the hashing seed / affinity mapping so some prefixes mapped to same shard. that would create hotspots and long tails for streaming, since warm KV caches are partitioned. streaming stalls line up with hot KV cache misses + queueing.

priya-eng: Confirmed. I can repro locally by applying the new seed config; it collapses ~14% of keys onto 2 nodes. this is a regression in the rollout. The policy had a fallback that should spread but it didn't because of an ordering bug in the policy comparator.

maria-oncall: mitigation options?

alex-runtime: immediate actions I can take now:
1) roll back cfg-2026-03-14-evict-affinity to previous stable (cfg-2026-03-07-affinity) -> should re-balance within 30-90s as routing tables converge
2) temporarily increase per-router concurrency limit on euw2-a-03 and euw2-a-02 to reduce rejection/backpressure (quick but masks root cause)
3) route a % of traffic away from euw2 to euw1 for heavier workloads (geo fallback), needs approval

maria-oncall: do 1) now. alex, trigger rollback. dan, prepare a hotshard evacuation plan. priya, hold the rollout. cara-cs, ping customers?

cara-cs: I'll notify affected enterprise accounts with a short note: "We're investigating elevated latency in EU region; mitigation in progress. You may see transient retries." Any known customers impacted?

pagerduty: maria-oncall acked the page at 09:18 UTC. automated status page entry created (incident #INC-20260315-014).

alex-runtime: rolling back config now: `POST /cfg/v1/rollbacks -d {"target":"cfg-2026-03-07-affinity"}`
[09:20:12] rollback started
[09:21:05] controlplane: rollout completed to euw2 controllers
[09:21:40] router telem: first steady-state signals returning. queue_depth on euw2-a-03 down to 18.

ops-alerts: metrics after rollback (09:30): p95=240ms, p99=490ms, streaming stalls ~0.15%. improvement visible across all stacks.

dan-sre: good. still want to perform a controlled evacuation of hot connections to ensure no lingering long-lived streams on euw2-a-03. plan: cordon router euw2-a-03 from new allocations, drain existing connections with 30s graceful period. I can start that at 09:40.

maria-oncall: do it. also let's block the offending rollout in CI and add a guard on the comparator ordering. priya, can you patch and open a rollback-proof test?

priya-eng: patching now. root cause: the comparator used for policy evaluation used an unstable map iteration order in go (we used map to sort priorities). test will seed deterministic order and add property test that 99.9% of hash keys don't change allocation for a given config change. pushing CL in 20m.

cara-cs: customer impact tracker:
- reported by 3 enterprise accounts (low volume but high SLA) via support at 09:19 UTC
- observed increased API retries reported by 18 developer orgs (self-serve)
- status page updated at 09:22 UTC
I'll send a follow-up with ETA once we confirm full recovery.

ops-alerts: live metrics (09:50): p95 230ms, p99 430ms, streaming stalls below baseline 0.05%. cordon/drain complete on euw2-a-03.

dan-sre: initiating post-rollback validation run: run synthetic workload to exercise long streaming sessions + token-by-token to ensure no stall recurrence. test script: 
```
for i in 1..200; do ./stream-test --region euw2 --duration 120 --prefix sample-$i & done
monitor logs for stall >= 5s
```

alex-runtime: running validation now; feeding results to observability. early look: no stalls observed in 600 streams so far.

maria-oncall: great. I'm going to de-escalate paging to notify only SRE rotation, but keep incident open for postmortem. cara, send note to impacted customers with mitigation summary + apology + follow-up timeframe for RCA.

cara-cs: drafting: "We experienced elevated latency in EU-WEST2 caused by a routing affinity policy rollout which created uneven traffic distribution. We rolled back the change, drained affected routers, and restored normal service. We're conducting an RCA and will follow up with details and compensatory credits where applicable." will send after you approve.

priya-eng: CL 4832 submitted: fix comparator ordering + deterministic seeding for policy rollout. adding unit+property tests. also adding a canary gating step that verifies weight distribution doesn't exceed 3x variance per shard during rollout.

dan-sre: follow-ups for postmortem:
- timeline with telemetry (ingress -> router -> queueing)
- why comparator took unstable order (code review + language guarantees)
- add automated canary that simulates prefix distribution to catch skew before global rollout
- add a runbook: hotshard evacuation checklist (cordon -> graceful drain -> redistribute -> verify metrics)

maria-oncall: I'll file the incident ticket INC-20260315-014 and add owners: priya-eng for fix, dan-sre for runbook, alex-runtime for validation infra, cara-cs for customer comms.

incident-bot: severity downgraded to SEV3 at 10:10 UTC. incident marked in-progress for RCA.

maria-oncall: thanks team. final notes: avoid heavy churn in affinity policy during business hours for EU region until we have the gating tests in place. I'll send a short summary to all-hands.

cara-cs: sent customer update at 10:22 UTC. responses: 1 follow-up asking for timeline for credits. I'll route to finance + support.

ops-alerts: closing metrics snapshot: p95=215ms, p99=410ms, streaming stalls normalized. incident window: 09:12 - 09:40 (major impact), residual validation until 10:30.

maria-oncall: closing thread for active mitigation. will keep incident ticket open for RCA completion. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
